Articles 79–122 – Parliament
Lok Sabha – 5 years
Rajya Sabha – Permanent
Minimum age: Lok Sabha – 25, Rajya Sabha – 30
Money Bill – Lok Sabha only
Joint sitting – Speaker presides
Three sessions of Parliament
Articles 124 to 147 of the Indian Constitution deal with the Supreme Court of India.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Articles 79 to 122 of the Constitution govern the Parliament of India.
Lok Sabha has a normal tenure of 5 years, whereas Rajya Sabha is a permanent body.
The minimum qualification age is 25 years for Lok Sabha and 30 years for Rajya Sabha.
Money Bills can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha.
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over joint sittings of Parliament.
Articles 124 to 147 deal with the Supreme Court of India and the Integrated Judiciary.
Money Bills are introduced exclusively in the Lok Sabha.
The Speaker presides over a Joint Sitting of both Houses of Parliament.
Rajya Sabha is a permanent body and not subject to dissolution.
Constitutional provisions for the Supreme Court fall under Articles 124–147.

blocks.content: Chapter 8: Supreme Court of India and Integrated Judiciary
Articles 124 to 147 of the Indian Constitution deal with the Supreme Court of India.
